I previously taught applied statistics and data analytics at the graduate and PhD level. All course material below is shared under the GNU General Public License (GPL-3) — use it, adapt it, teach from it.

As I teach new courses that can be shared, I'll include those here.

## Courses

::: {.card-grid}
::: {.tile}
### Statistical Foundations
PhD-level. The foundations sequence: probability, estimation, inference, t-tests, ANOVA, and others.

[Course materials →](teaching/foundations.qmd){.tile-link}
:::

::: {.tile}
### Regression Analysis
PhD-level. Regression, including OLS, generalized linear models, diagnostics, interactions, splines, and more.

[Course materials →](teaching/regression.qmd){.tile-link}
:::

::: {.tile}
### Applied Statistical Analysis
Graduate-level applied course, taught with both R and Jamovi so the statistics are not gated behind the syntax.

[Course materials →](teaching/applied.qmd){.tile-link}
:::

::: {.tile}
### Intro and Intermediate R
Graduate-level R sequence — from first script to a reproducible analysis pipeline.

[Course materials →](teaching/rcourse.qmd){.tile-link}
:::

::: {.tile}
### Research Methods in Psychology
Undergraduate. The whole research process, from question formulation to communicating results.

[Course materials →](teaching/psychmethods.qmd){.tile-link}
:::

::: {.tile}
### Supporting resources
Jamovi tutorials, REDCap guides, and *R for Researchers*.

[Jamovi](teaching/jamovi.qmd){.tile-link} ·
[REDCap](teaching/redcap.qmd){.tile-link} ·
[R for Researchers](teaching/r4research.qmd){.tile-link}
:::
